purpose: Teach: 宅地/本数/常々/急行/チャージ/有給/待ち時間/少額

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 創業時、私の自宅、当時、宅地の一部に、社屋、建てたんだぞ、覚えてる、お前?
lines.en: When we were founding this place, I built the office right on part of my own residential land. You remember that, don't you?
lines.style: Measured, deliberate. Opens with quiet certainty. Pauses between phrases—not rushed, like he's choosing each word with care. Slight upward lilt on the question, genuinely asking if he knows.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: はい。創業期、社員、本数、片手で、数えられたって、お母さんから、聞いてます、本当に、絶対、すごい歴史です。
lines.en: Yes. I've heard from your mother how small the staff was back then—you could count them on one hand. It really is an incredible history.
lines.style: Respectful, attentive. Sits forward slightly in his posture. Warm but formal—the tone of someone honoring what an elder has built. Steady eye contact, no rushing through the praise.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 常々、お父さんから、お前に、伝えたかったこと、たくさん、あるぞ、いつか、ゆっくり、話したいな、絶対。
lines.en: There's so much I've always wanted to tell you about, so many things your father wanted to pass down. I'd like to tell you the full story someday, slowly, when we have time.
lines.style: Tender, almost wistful. Softens around the edges. Spoken as if confessing a long-held wish. Slight catch of vulnerability—this matters to him. Trails very gently on 'someday.'

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: はい。お父さん、急行で、創業祭の会場、お見送りに、参ります、絶対、お楽しみに、ね、本当に、絶対。
lines.en: Yes, I will make sure to see you off at the founding anniversary celebration. Please look forward to it—truly, I'm looking forward to it myself.
lines.style: Warm, genuine commitment. Leans in with sincerity. Speaks as if making a personal promise. Rhythm is assured but not stiff—the rhythm of someone who means what they're saying.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 創業期、銀行から、チャージ、お金を、借りる時、本当に、苦労したんだぞ、若い君に、伝えたい、絶対。
lines.en: When we were starting out, getting loans from the bank was incredibly hard. I really struggled with that, and I want you to understand that difficulty, now that you're taking over.
lines.style: Direct, grounded. Voice carries weight—not aggressive, but serious. Pauses after difficult words, letting them land. The cadence of someone passing on a hard-won lesson, not complaining.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: はい。お父さんも、有給、しっかり、取って、ゆっくり、過ごしてくださいね、本当に、お願い、絶対、健康、第一に。
lines.en: Yes. Please make sure to take your vacation time properly and rest—truly, I'm asking you to put your health first above everything else.
lines.style: Gentle but firm. Not pleading, but sincere concern underneath. Speaks with quiet insistence, as if this matters as much as the business talk. Almost paternal in its care.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: お客様の待ち時間、創業時、私たち、必死で、減らしたぞ、お父さんから、お前にも、伝統、引き継いで欲しい、絶対。
lines.en: When we were founding this company, we worked desperately to reduce how long customers had to wait. That's a tradition I want you to inherit from me—the commitment to never letting customers wait.
lines.style: Resolute, almost grave. Sits taller. Speaks with quiet authority about what was fought for. The tone of passing down something sacred, something earned. Emphasis on 'desperately' and 'wait,' not rushed.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: はい。少額の経費から、丁寧に、扱うこと、創業者として、お父さんの、教え、絶対、守ってまいります、本当に。
lines.en: Yes. Treating even the smallest expenses with care and respect—that's the founder's way, that's what you taught me, and I will absolutely uphold that teaching.
lines.style: Steady, respectful. Voice carries both humility and conviction. Spoken as a vow rather than a statement. Slight pause before 'absolutely'—settling into the weight of the promise. Warm but assured.
